workstream: E04 — anchor-free phase coverage (burst-aware apex ownership) without weakening physical-ordering invariants or honest abstention
environment: Linux, Node 20, pnpm; no Apple Vision / Mac / iPhone (not needed). Held-out cases wm-dink-01 / afn-vic-rally1 were never read, labeled, or touched (they have no bundles under datasets/paddle-bench/runs-wave-a).
baseline_note: The task brief quoted 6/13 anchor-free coverage (D3-05 v2.2 measurement); on the CURRENT wave-c-integration gold (datasets/paddle-bench/stroke-gold.json grew since D3-05) the same measurement script (datasets/experiments/wave-d3/d3-05-measure-gold.ts, unmodified) gives 8/18 anchor-free and 15/17 anchored before this change. Both baselines are honest measurements of different gold snapshots.

forensics.method: datasets/experiments/wave-e/e04-forensics.ts (committed, read-only over committed wave-a bundles): for each anchor-free abstained gold case, dump in-event peak, padded/in-event medians, margin maximum + its burst separation from the apex (minimum series value between them vs the boundary-walking accel threshold), rival peaks, sample counts, max inter-sample gap.
forensics.finding: 5 of 10 abstentions were PHASE_PEAK_OUTSIDE_EVENT / rival-driven where the contesting sample sits in the ±300ms margin and is REST-SEPARATED from the in-event apex (series drops below 0.25× the smaller contesting peak between them) — i.e. it is the NEIGHBORING stroke of a dense dink/volley rally, not this event's apex. The v2.2 ownership/rival gates judged every margin sample as if it belonged to this event's swing.

change.what: segmentPhasesAnchorFree v2.3: the apex-ownership gate (PHASE_PEAK_OUTSIDE_EVENT) and the rival gate (PHASE_PEAK_NOT_UNIQUE) now EXEMPT margin samples that are rest-separated from the in-event apex — the series drops below 0.25 x min(apex, contender) (the exact boundary-walking accel-threshold criterion the module already uses for 'the swing motion has ended') somewhere between the two samples. In-event samples ALWAYS contest (periodic in-event motion — the D3-05 B2 wheelchair break — still abstains); a margin peak motion-connected to the apex is the same swing spilling past the event boundary and still abstains.
change.not_weakened: no threshold, floor, denominator, or sample-count gate changed; the anchored path is untouched (byte-identical, regression-pinned tests still pass); the B2 wheelchair fixture (event covering multiple pushes) still abstains; PHASE_TEMPORAL_V2_ANCHOR_FREE_VERSION re-versioned v2.2 -> v2.3 because abstention semantics changed (contract versioned, not softened in place).

coverage_before_after.measurement: datasets/experiments/wave-d3/d3-05-measure-gold.ts unmodified, on committed wave-a gold (18 anchor-free-eligible labels across 8 dev bundles; grouped by source clip, no random-frame splits; held-out-free)
coverage_before_after.validity: all 12 segmented anchor-free outputs pass ordering + checkArtifactInvariants (asserted by the new test suite's shared expectOrderedAnchorFree helper on identical synthetic reproductions; the D3-05 measure script reports status only, and every segmented gold case flows through the same monotonicity gate that abstains PHASE_DISORDERED_BOUNDARIES)

fuzz.d3_05_corruption_fuzz: datasets/experiments/wave-d3/d3-05-measure-fuzz.ts unmodified: 147 segmented (145 anchored / 2 anchor-free) — IDENTICAL before and after this change; the 10 multi-modal random-walk abstentions B2 introduced are all preserved
fuzz.e04_two_burst_fuzz: new 300-seed deterministic two-burst rally fuzz (test/phaseAnchorFree.test.ts): every segmented output passes ordering + checkArtifactInvariants after JSON round-trip; abstentions all carry named reasons

residual_risk_disclosed: if an event selector bounds EXACTLY ONE push of a periodic motion (so all rival pushes fall outside the event and outside motion-connection), v2.3 will segment around that push where v2.2 abstained. On committed gold this does not occur (the wheelchair case keeps an in-event rival and still abstains). The event-local contract already delegates 'is this a stroke event' to the selector; noted here rather than hidden.
